explanation: I found no Mathlib duplicate; I did not search Mathlib, because the statement is built entirely from the library's own definitions. These are `CopyScheduleRole`, `atomIntervalRanges`, `initialWordAtomLower`/`initialWordAtomUpper`, `initialWordBinRanges`, `primeSubsetPrior` and `initialWordTupleEquiv`, all in the OAI.Ostmann construction. Mathlib has no counterparts to these. The proof is a one-line wrapper that combines two other library lemmas, `initialWordAtomIntervals_equiv` and `initialWordPrior_cell_product_bounds`, and neither is from Mathlib. Since all of the mathematical content sits in the library's own definitions, no Mathlib, Batteries or Lean core declaration can duplicate it.
